name: Will I need to replace my toilet if the flange is damaged?

mainEntity.name: Will I need to replace my toilet if the flange is damaged?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. In most cases, a damaged toilet flange can be repaired or replaced without needing to purchase a new toilet. The primary goal is to ensure a stable, watertight connection between your existing toilet and the drainpipe. However, if the toilet itself is very old, cracked, or experiencing other issues, a plumber might recommend replacement alongside the flange repair as a more cost-effective long-term solution. CG Plumbing Solutions can advise on the best approach based on the condition of both components.
acceptedAnswer.description: Often, only the flange needs repair or replacement, not the toilet itself, unless the toilet is also damaged or very old.
